pharmacy_refill_law: Standing emergency refill is a 72-hour supply; a governor's emergency proclamation can extend it to a 30-day supply. Not for Schedule I/II drugs.

Up to a 30-day emergency refill (non-controlled) when the governor declares a state of emergency under A.R.S. § 32-1910(A)/(B); a second 30-day refill is allowed if the emergency continues 21+ days. Ends when the declaration is terminated.

During a proclaimed state of emergency, a pharmacist may refill a prescription without the prescriber's authorization if the prescriber is unavailable after a reasonable effort to contact them; the statute sets no fixed days-supply cap for this provision specifically (Bus. & Prof. Code § 4064).

Up to a 30-day supply once a county is under an NWS hurricane warning or a gubernatorial state-of-emergency order (Fla. Stat. § 465.0275, pharmacist side); insurers must also waive refill-too-soon restrictions and cover the 30 days (Fla. Stat. § 252.358).

Up to a 30-day supply once the governor declares a state of emergency or the NWS issues a hurricane warning for the area, per O.C.G.A. § 26-4-80(j) and the Board of Pharmacy's standing Policy #14; not for Schedule II. Prescriber notified within 48 hours.
Up to a 30-day supply (non-controlled) when the governor issues an executive order under KRS 39A.100 activating pharmacists' emergency authority under KRS 315.500, per KRS 217.215(3).
Up to a 30-day supply once the governor declares or renews a state of emergency, under Louisiana Board of Pharmacy Rule §519 ('State of Emergency'), automatically activated by the declaration.

Up to a 30-day supply during a federal or state emergency declaration when the prescriber cannot be reached (versus 14 days normally); prescriber notified within 7 days. Not for controlled substances. Health Occ. § 12-506.

Only a 72-hour supply, triggered when a natural or man-made disaster itself prevents the pharmacist from contacting the prescriber (Admin. Code Ph 703.10 / RSA 318:47-f) — New Hampshire does not extend this to 30 days the way most PHE-specific states do.

Insurers must allow and cover an early refill for up to 29 days after the Dept. of Insurance issues a bulletin following an emergency declaration (N.C.G.S. § 58-3-228) — an insurance-coverage guarantee alongside the separate pharmacist-side refill rule.

Up to a 30-day supply of a non-controlled medication when the prescriber cannot be reached and the pharmacist judges it essential to health/safety; controlled substances capped at 10 days (63 O.S. § 2-309 and Board rule).
Up to a 30-day supply during a declared emergency when the drug is essential to health or continuing therapy (versus 72 hours outside a declared emergency) — OAR 855-041-1120 / 855-007-0090.

A one-time emergency refill of up to a 30-day supply during a declared State of Emergency, marked 'Emergency Refill' and the prescriber notified within 15 days. Not for controlled substances. S.C. Code § 40-43-170.

Up to a 30-day supply (non-Schedule-II) when a natural/man-made disaster prevents contacting the prescriber, the governor has declared a state of disaster under Govt. Code Ch. 418, and the Board has issued its own notification. Tex. Occ. Code § 562.054.
Up to a 30-day supply of legend (non-controlled) drugs, or 7 days for Schedule III-V, once the governor issues an emergency proclamation preventing continuity of care. WAC 246-945-332.
